# S100 — Bell: ring when a run ends, and a per-project bell setting

The TUI rings the terminal bell once when a run of a project ends (an ork engine run reaching `committed` or `stopped`, or a ledger-only relay run reaching `ended`), and every bell of a project stops when its registry field `bell` is `false`. The field is read from `projects.json`; the command `ork projects set NAME --bell on|off` is a separate slice (E-class, see the manifest).

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

## Why

S07 once promised a bell with the live role detail. The premise was checked on 2026-10-28 and again at HEAD of main: the bell already ships (`ui.notify`, adj 44, decided "bell": terminal bell and tab badge). `Model.apply` rings it once when a project's open adj count or held-item count rises past an earlier good reading (`internal/tui/model.go:1067-1131`; `Config.Bell`, default writes BEL to stderr, `internal/tui/model.go:51,207-209`); the paragraph is `docs/dashboard.md:399`. Two things are not in the code: a bell when a run ends, and any per-project switch (`rg -n bell internal/registry` finds nothing). The ring on a rise does not cover a run that pauses, awaits approval or stops: those are Needs-you rows but not part of the rise check.

Owner decisions of 2026-10-28 (interactive, recorded in the slice note): (1) also ring once when a run ends (pass, fail, stopped or landed); (2) the bell stays on by default and is switched per project with a registry field `bell` (*proposed*, on when unset), set with `ork projects set NAME --bell on|off`. The slice re-reads both against the code:

- "Ends" for an ork engine run is `runrec.IsFinal` (`internal/runrec/record.go:39`): state `committed` (a landed or committed slice) or `stopped`. "Pass, fail" are the ledger outcomes of a relay run, which slicer reports as state `ended` with outcome `pass`, `fail` or `stopped` (`internal/slicercli/types.go:171-181`; `internal/tui/relayboard.go` reads `ended`). An ork engine run and its ledger run are one run: the ledger run named by `EngineRun.RelayRun` is not counted again (the same de-duplication `projectState.needs` uses, `internal/tui/model.go:85-100`).
- Ledger runs that ork did not start (an outer session's relays) end the same way and come from `Snapshot.BoardRuns` (stale and the last hour of ended runs, `internal/source/source.go:80`, `:322-324`).
- The split of the setting from its command: `ork projects set` always goes through the daemon (`setProject`, `internal/daemon/handlers.go:513`), so the command is E-class. This slice stays out of `internal/daemon` so it can run beside an E-class slice in a pair wave (owner, 2026-10-31: pair waves allow one E-class slice).

Registry key (exact): `bell`, a JSON boolean, optional. Absent or `true` means the bell is on; `false` means every bell for that project is off. The registry loads with strict keys, so an ork older than this slice refuses a `projects.json` that has `bell` (same note as `ui_doc` and `ui_pass_skills`, `docs/state.md:93-95`).

Limit: the TUI reads the registry once at start (`cmd/ork/main.go:188`), so a running TUI keeps the value it read; restart `ork` to apply an edit.

## Failing tests

In `internal/registry/registry_test.go`:

- TestRegistryBellFieldDefaultsOn: a project with no `bell` key has `BellOn()` true and `Bell == nil`; `"bell":false` round-trips through `Load` and `Save` and `BellOn()` is false; `"bell":true` round-trips as true; a nil `Bell` writes no `bell` key. Fails first: no field.

In `internal/tui/bell_test.go`:

- TestBellRingsWhenAnEngineRunEnds: a project whose first reading has an engine run in `implement` rings nothing; a later reading that has the same run `committed` rings once; the same for `stopped`; further identical readings ring nothing.
- TestBellRingsWhenALedgerOnlyRunEnds: a board run (state `active`, then `ended` with outcome `fail`) with no engine run linked to it rings once when it ends.
- TestBellRingsOnceForALinkedEngineAndLedgerRun: an engine run with `RelayRun: "run-1"` and a board run `run-1` that both end in one reading ring once, and in two readings still once.
- TestBellDoesNotRingForARunAlreadyEndedAtStart: the first good reading holds an ended engine run and an ended board run: no ring; a second identical reading: no ring.
- TestBellEndedRunsBaselineAgainAfterSetup: a reading with no `.slicer/` (the setup state, `isSetup`) clears the memory, so runs that are ended in the next reading ring nothing.
- TestBellFailedBoardReadKeepsTheEndedRunsAndRingsNothing: a reading whose `BoardRuns` call failed does not ring, does not forget the ids, and the next good reading with the same ended runs rings nothing.
- TestBellRingsOncePerSnapshot: a reading in which the open count rises and a run ends rings once (one `Config.Bell` call).
- TestBellStillRingsWhenCountRises: the existing rule is unchanged for a project with the bell on (the cases of `tui_test.go:1163` stay green; this test covers the held count as well).
- TestBellOffForAProjectWithBellOff: with `Bell` false in the project's registry entry, no ring for a count rise, a held rise or a run end; the sidebar badge and counts still update; a second project with the bell on still rings.
- TestBellOnWhenTheFieldIsAbsentOrTrue: both rings.

## Implement

1. Write the failing tests first and run them; each must fail for the reason given.
2. `internal/registry/registry.go`: `Bell *bool` and `func (p Project) BellOn() bool { return p.Bell == nil || *p.Bell }`. No validator: a bool needs none. Do not add a flag, a wire field or a daemon change here.
3. `internal/tui/model.go`: add to `projectState` an `ended map[string]bool`, and the flags `hasEngineEnds` and `hasBoardEnds`. In `apply`, outside the `isSetup` branch:
   - collect the ended ids: engine runs (skip `Unavailable`) whose `State` satisfies `runrec.IsFinal`, keyed `engine:ID`; and, when `snap.BoardRuns.Err == nil`, board runs with `State == "ended"` whose `ID` is not the `RelayRun` of any engine run in the snapshot, keyed `ledger:ID`;
   - for each part, the first good reading only fills `ended` and sets its flag; a later good reading with an id not in `ended` sets `ended-rose` and adds it; a failed `BoardRuns` read changes nothing;
   - in the `isSetup` branch, clear `ended` and both flags with the counts.
   Then `if (rose || endedRose) && ps.reg.BellOn() { ring once }`; the existing count bookkeeping runs whether or not the bell is on. Keep the existing `rose` logic as it is.
4. Docs: `docs/dashboard.md:26,399` (the bell rings on a rising count and when a run ends; a project with `bell: false` rings nothing; counts and badges still update; the TUI reads the setting at start); `docs/state.md` (the example gets `"bell": false` on the second line of the project or a comment line; a field note: optional boolean, on when absent, per project, older ork refuses the key, `ork projects set NAME --bell on|off` lands with the setter slice); `docs/guide.md:376-377`.
5. `CHANGELOG.md`, last (so a parallel slice's entry does not conflict): one entry at the top of `## Unreleased`, marked *proposed* (beyond the roadmap: the registry key).
